counters.note: Real user-space per-thread counters (exclude_kernel=1), reset/enabled around each measured loop, disabled before reading. `missing_counters` maps each event this microarchitecture/PMU does not expose to the exact errno/reason the kernel returned (e.g. EINVAL for an unsupported generic TLB event); those counters are skipped by name, never reported as zero and never conflated with an unavailable PMU. When the container profile denies perf_event_open the whole section records available:false with the exact errno and every probe reports measured:false with wall-clock time only — no counter is fabricated.

manifest_handle_allocations.note: latest_for_shared (the read path) allocates nothing per call; the deep-cloning latest_for allocates the manifest's owned fields. Before Phase 50 the read path used latest_for: the court measured 8.0 allocs/read, dropping to 2.0 after the change.

note: Single-run, single-host microarchitecture probes. The **proxies** (a counting global allocator for hot-path allocator traffic, concurrent-reader throughput for the remaining shared-lock surface, and a working-set latency curve as a cache-hierarchy shape) need no PMU and run in every container. Under the probed PERFMON profile (scripts/container-microarch.sh) the `counters` section additionally carries **real** user-space hardware counters for each hot-path component (cycles, instructions, cache-references/-misses, branch-misses, and the DTLB/ITLB read misses where the PMU exposes them). A counter the microarchitecture does not provide is skipped by name; when the container profile denies perf_event_open the section records available:false with the exact errno and only wall-clock times are reported — the default container's seccomp profile denies the syscall with EPERM, which is **not** the paranoid level (perf_event_paranoid=2 permits user-space counters; see docs/PMU.md). Absolute nanoseconds are host/load sensitive; the shape, the allocator counts, and the counter ratios are the point.

pmu.note: Environment metadata. perf_event_paranoid=2 permits user-space per-thread counters; the real gate is the container seccomp profile, which denies perf_event_open with EPERM in the default container. Run under --cap-add PERFMON to read the counters (see docs/PMU.md).

reader_scaling_baseline.note: Phase 50 replaced the per-path served counter (an RwLock<HashMap>) with a lock-free atomic array, removing the last policy write lock from the served-read path.

steady_state_read_allocations.interpretation: A steady-state certified read returns one result Vec; the read planner adds no per-read manifest clone (Phase 50 shares the published manifest as an Arc).
